nodes.label: liberu-module Composer Package Type
nodes.rationale: Every foundation and product module declares package type `liberu-module` so the host can discover it as a composition unit rather than as an ordinary Composer library.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/composer-installer
nodes.rationale: A trusted installer places each package at /modules/<installer-name> so the install path is deterministic and the host can track the directory in Git while Composer and its lock file stay the source of version truth.

nodes.label: Installation Does Not Imply Enablement
nodes.rationale: Every README repeats that 'installation does not imply runtime enablement or commercial entitlement'. Enablement is a separate explicit decision driven by the manifest, so shipping a package never boots it.

nodes.label: Capability Boundary Integration
nodes.rationale: Hosts integrate a package through its declared capabilities and public contracts rather than application-specific classes; consumers must not couple to internal tables or classes.

nodes.label: Category: foundation
nodes.rationale: Foundation-category packages are presentation-neutral domain cores.

nodes.label: Category: presentation
nodes.rationale: Presentation-category packages carry Filament, Livewire or HTTP-API surfaces so domain cores stay UI-agnostic.

nodes.label: Packagist Names Omit the module- Prefix
nodes.rationale: Source repositories use the `module-` GitHub prefix; Composer and Packagist package names intentionally omit it, so `liberusoftware/module-search` on GitHub is `liberusoftware/search` on Packagist.

nodes.label: Tracked modules/ Directory with Composer as Version Truth
nodes.rationale: The installed directory stays tracked by the host repository so the composition is reproducible from Git, while Composer and its lock file remain the authority on versions.

nodes.label: Private Security Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities go to security@liberusoftware.com rather than public GitHub issues so a report can be handled before disclosure.

nodes.label: Shared users Table
nodes.rationale: No package owns the users table; several packages extend it with their own migrations, which is the one place where the per-package persistence boundary is deliberately shared.

nodes.label: Sanctum Bearer Security Scheme
nodes.rationale: Every versioned API adapter declares a single global `sanctum` HTTP bearer scheme so authentication is uniform across the fleet's OpenAPI contracts.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key Header (x-liberu-idempotency-header)
nodes.rationale: A vendor OpenAPI extension pins the idempotency header name at the contract level so retried writes are safe without each adapter inventing its own convention.

nodes.label: Versioned openapi/v1 Adapter Contract
nodes.rationale: Each -api module carries its own OpenAPI 3.1 document under openapi/v1/, so the HTTP contract is versioned independently of the domain package it adapts.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla
nodes.rationale: Independent, team-scoped Zoopla synchronization core. It deliberately does not depend on the portal-reporting module; provider credentials and transport belong in replaceable integration services so the core stays free of vendor coupling.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla API
nodes.rationale: Independent versioned API adapter for Zoopla sync records, kept separate from the domain core.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla Filament
nodes.rationale: Independent Filament 5 adapter, so the Zoopla domain core ships no admin UI of its own.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla Livewire
nodes.rationale: Independent Livewire 4 adapter for Zoopla synchronization records.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla Sync API (OpenAPI v1)
Liberu Roles and Permissions
nodes.rationale: Owns contextual role assignments, module-owned permissions, policies and cache invalidation as the fleet's single authorization core.

nodes.label: Liberu Authorization Filament
nodes.rationale: Filament role and permission management is a separate presentation package so the authorization core carries no Filament dependency.

nodes.label: Liberu Scheduler and Queues
nodes.rationale: Centralises unique/idempotent job policy, schedules, locks, retries, failures, monitoring and graceful deployment conventions so each module does not re-derive them.

nodes.label: Liberu Search
nodes.rationale: Authorized search queries, filters, pagination and replaceable model configuration; model configuration is replaceable so the search core does not hardcode the host's searchable models.

nodes.label: Liberu Search API
nodes.rationale: Authenticated, rate-limited HTTP endpoints kept in a presentation package so the search core stays transport-agnostic.

nodes.label: Liberu Sessions and Devices
nodes.rationale: Privacy-conscious active-session inventory with current-session protection, so revoking sessions cannot lock the acting user out of their own session.

nodes.label: Liberu Sessions and Devices Administration
nodes.rationale: Accessible account security and preferences surface targeted at the app panel rather than the admin panel.

nodes.label: Liberu Settings
nodes.rationale: Typed application, organization, team/site and user settings with validation and deterministic cache invalidation — determinism matters because settings are read on every request path.

nodes.label: Liberu Settings Administration
nodes.rationale: Optional Filament settings administration surface; optional so a headless composition can consume settings without Filament.

nodes.label: Liberu Theme Support
nodes.rationale: Theme discovery, view overrides, safe asset directives, preferences and panel palettes. Asset directives are 'safe' because themes are third-party packages whose declared assets must be validated before rendering.

nodes.label: Liberu Theme Support Livewire
nodes.rationale: Interactive theme selection isolated in a Livewire presentation package.

nodes.label: Liberu Two-Factor Authentication
nodes.rationale: TOTP enforcement, trusted-device policy and single-use recovery primitives; recovery codes are single-use so a leaked code cannot be replayed.

nodes.label: Liberu Webhooks
nodes.rationale: Endpoint registration, signing, filtering, delivery evidence, backoff, rotation, replay and logs. Delivery evidence and replay exist so an undelivered event is provable and recoverable rather than silently lost.

nodes.label: PrivilegedActor Contract
nodes.rationale: The only public contract the authorization core exports, so a host model declares privilege without importing the package's internals.

nodes.label: ThemeValidateCommand
nodes.rationale: Themes are third-party packages whose declared assets must exist; validation is a first-class command rather than a build-time assumption.

nodes.label: create_break_glass_grants_table Migration
nodes.rationale: Break-glass grants give the authorization core an auditable emergency-elevation path distinct from ordinary role assignment.

nodes.label: create_sessions_table Migration
nodes.rationale: Dated 0001_01_01 so Laravel's core sessions table is created before any package migration that depends on it.

nodes.label: create_scoped_settings_table Migration
nodes.rationale: Scoped settings is the persistence behind the organization / team-site / user tiers layered over spatie/laravel-settings' single global store.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/module-manager
nodes.rationale: The manifest/registry package that every foundation module requires, so discovery and dependency resolution have one owner.

nodes.label: spatie/laravel-permission ^7.0
nodes.rationale: Pinned to ^7.0; a v8 upgrade is blocked by filament-shield ~4.x requiring ^6.0|^7.0.

nodes.label: Liberu Application Composition
nodes.rationale: Composes the Liberu boilerplate foundation with project-relevant Real Estate core, API, Filament and Livewire modules. Foundation packages stay reusable and presentation-neutral; Real Estate packages are selected one-to-one across the four implementation indexes. Deferred frontend indexes are out of scope for this run.

nodes.label: Liberu Platform Scope
nodes.rationale: Cross-product Liberu modules are added to this scope only when not already owned by the application foundation or a product scope, preventing duplicate ownership of a capability.

nodes.label: Liberu API Modules Scope
nodes.rationale: Shared API access, webhooks, integrations, import/export and readiness contracts come from foundation packages; product APIs remain under their owning project scope.

nodes.label: Liberu Core Modules Scope
nodes.rationale: Names the foundation core packages the current application consumes: application, identity, organizations and teams, settings, audit, search, notifications, files and media, observability, scheduler and queues, and supporting contracts.

nodes.label: Four Implementation Indexes (core / api / filament / livewire)
nodes.rationale: Every product domain is published as a one-to-one set of four packages — domain core plus API, Filament and Livewire adapters — so presentation choice never forces a domain dependency.
